title: Refill-Too-Soon Edit — Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit Provider Manual
content:
**Edit.** On the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, a refill of the same drug rejects as too soon until the network's refill fraction of the previous paid fill's days supply has elapsed, counting the previous date of service as day zero. The fraction for a drug that is not a controlled substance and the fraction for a controlled substance are each set by the network.

**Accumulation.** Even when that fraction has elapsed, a refill rejects when the extra days supply accumulated by earlier-than-due refills of the same drug within the network's accumulation window would exceed the network's accumulation limit.

**Override.** A refill that rejects as too soon is paid only under an override granted by the override rules.

## How the accumulated days are counted

The accumulated days are the sum, over the member's paid and unreversed retail claims for the same drug, of the days by which each fill came before the date its prior fill's full days supply ran out. The window is a rolling count of calendar days ending on the date of service being evaluated.

## Day counting (hypothetical fills)

| Previous fill | Fraction | Earliest day of refill (previous date of service is day zero) | Refill on the day before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 days, drug not controlled | 0.8 | Day 24 | Day 23 rejects as too soon |
| 30 days, drug not controlled | 0.75 | Day 23 (22.5 days must elapse) | Day 22 rejects as too soon |
| 30 days, controlled substance | 0.9 | Day 27 | Day 26 rejects as too soon |

## Accumulation case (hypothetical)

On a network whose accumulation limit is 7 days, a member's earlier refills of lisinopril within the window came a total of 5 days before their prior fills ran out. A further refill that passes the fraction but comes 3 days before the prior fill runs out would bring the accumulated days to 8, which exceeds 7, so it rejects. Had it come 2 days early, the total of 7 would not exceed the limit and the refill would not reject on accumulation.
